tickets.what: Charged with assaulting two bailiffs, criminal damage and wanton or furious driving after the November 1988 eviction.
tickets.detail: Taken from his bed at Llandough Hospital on 3 Dec 1988 to face the charges and bailed on 9 Dec. A separate threatening-behaviour summons for the 29 Apr 1988 stand-off was withdrawn in January 1989 as out of time. He pleaded guilty to the remaining charges and was freed on 23–24 Mar 1989.
tickets.fine: No record found yet. The press records the guilty plea and his release, not a fine, fee or costs figure. The magistrates’ court file has not been traced (Ministry of Justice FOIA 260805002: no information held).

sources.title: Press: “Charge against evicted farmer dropped” (N12, Jan 1989)
Press: South Wales Echo, 24 Mar 1989, “farmer freed” (N15-16)

tickets.calibration: Three summary charges, admitted, dealt with by magistrates: 20,000 points, the middle of the Exceeding authority / summary offence band. Every other ticket is scored against this one.

tickets.what: Threatening-behaviour summons for the 29 Apr 1988 stand-off: withdrawn, out of time.
tickets.detail: The Crown Prosecution Service withdrew the summons at Barry magistrates’ court because it was out of time. Ticket cancelled: 0 points.

tickets.what: High Court possession order (Order 14) for “the whole of the farm”.
tickets.detail: Western Ground Rents sued Frederick alone and obtained summary judgment for possession of the whole farm. Enforced on 4 Jul 1955: every part except the farmhouse and garden was taken.

tickets.what: Cardiff County Court possession order for the farmhouse, buildings and garden. Not enforced.
tickets.detail: The order covered the occupied house group inside Parcel A. It was not enforced; in 1974 leave to enforce it was granted and the warrant then withdrawn.

tickets.what: High Court judgment for BP Properties Ltd: possession of Great House Farm, suspended six months.
tickets.detail: Writ served 22 May 1984; hearing 10 Jul 1986; judgment 24 Jul 1986 for BP, possession suspended for six months.

sources.title: GHF-E140 — High Court hearing and judgment, 1986

tickets.what: Court of Appeal dismisses the appeal: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2.
tickets.detail: The appeal on possession, limitation and the 1974 letters was dismissed. The order for possession stood.

tickets.what: House of Lords refuses leave to appeal.
tickets.detail: With leave refused, the 1987 judgment became final and BP moved to evict on 29 Apr 1988.

sources.title: GHF-E142 — House of Lords petition for leave, papers

tickets.what: European Commission of Human Rights declares application 14464/88 inadmissible.
tickets.detail: The Commission accepted that the possession order interfered with his home but held it lawful and justified. Four months after the house was gone.

tickets.what: Frederick’s tenancy was never put in writing, though a written agreement was intended.
tickets.detail: The 1987 Court of Appeal judgment records: “It was intended that Mr Frederick Buckler should have a written tenancy agreement, but this did not happen.”

tickets.what: Order for “the whole of the farm” made against Frederick alone; Mary, living in the Parcel A farmhouse, was not a party.
tickets.detail: Procedural point: a summary Order 14 judgment against one tenant was worded to cover the whole farm, including land occupied by a person who was never joined or heard.

tickets.what: Enforcing the 1955 order, it took the Parcel A woodland north of the house and the south-east ground (later village green VG41) along with Parcel B.
tickets.detail: The family’s established case: the “whole farm” wording blurred the 1877/1928 division between Parcel A and Parcel B, and Parcel A land went with the Parcel B taking.

tickets.what: The 1969 deed from Western Ground Rents is missing from the Land Registry files.
tickets.detail: The deed is not on the first-registration schedule. The missing 1969 root deed and the 1971 abstract are a gap in the chain of title.

sources.title: BP Properties Ltd and BP Pension Trust — Forensic Assessment

tickets.what: Mary pleaded ownership under the Limitation Act 1939; the case was part-heard and never relisted, so her plea was never decided.
tickets.detail: Procedural point: a defence of ownership was pleaded and left undecided. Nineteen weeks later the licence letters went out instead of the plea being tried.

sources.title: GHF-E135 — Mary’s plea of ownership and the pleadings, 1974

tickets.issued_to: BP Pension Trust Ltd and BP Properties Ltd
tickets.what: Warrant withdrawn and “licence” letters sent the same day, while Mary’s ownership plea was undecided.
tickets.detail: BP Properties then held only a contract to buy (its conveyance is dated 23 May 1975). The Court of Appeal later held the letters made her possession permissive although she never accepted them.

multipliers.why: done while a court or Strasbourg process was still running

tickets.what: BP’s first registrations went through while the family lived in the farmhouse; notice reached the family only after Mary died on 26 Mar 1983.
tickets.detail: Applications WA231076 (received 30 Nov 1982, Linklaters & Paines for BP Properties) and WA240304 (23 Feb 1983). The procedural question: what notice was served, on whom, and what chance there was to object.

tickets.what: The two titles were amalgamated on an application of 2 Feb 1987, while the appeal was still running.
tickets.detail: Open questions on the record: what was amalgamated, on which plans, and whether the court or the parties were told while the appeal was pending.

multipliers.why: done while a court or Strasbourg process was still running

tickets.what: Held that 1974 licence letters Mary never accepted made her possession permissive and stopped her limitation clock.
tickets.detail: Procedural point, citing the judgment: “It may be that the result would have been different if Mrs Buckler had, as soon as she learned of the letters, plainly told BP Properties Ltd that she did not accept the letters … she did not, however, do that.” Mary had died in 1983 and could not give evidence on it.

sources.title: EV-0080 — BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2

tickets.what: Smashed the gate lock and broke the doors with poleaxes; an axe came through a door with children behind it.
tickets.detail: Five bailiffs and about 15 police; a four-hour stand-off before the bailiffs backed off. The children were aged two, three and four.

sources.title: Press: “Chainsaw farmer vows to fight on” (N07, c. 30 Apr 1988)

tickets.what: Forced entry at Great House Farm; the householder was injured and taken to Llandough Hospital.
tickets.detail: “Angry scenes as farmer evicted” (South Wales Echo front page). The bailiffs had already taken half the roof off one of the outbuildings.

tickets.what: Demolition began within hours of the bailiffs forcing entry.
tickets.detail: The South Wales Echo of 3 Dec 1988 reported demolition starting within hours, and a High Court interim injunction that the farmhouse and its contents must not be touched.

sources.title: Press: “History fight to save farm” (N08, 3 Dec 1988)

tickets.what: A pregnant family member was dragged by her arms, kicked and put over the farm gate by the removal team; her shoulder was dislocated.
tickets.detail: The family’s own testimony of the 1988 removal: she went to the house to get medicine. Catalogued on the Legal Wiki as GHF-E114.

tickets.what: The householder was taken from his hospital bed to be charged.
tickets.detail: The South Wales Echo reported William taken from his bed at Llandough Hospital to face charges of assaulting two bailiffs (see the original ticket).

tickets.what: Refused an injunction to keep the house standing until Strasbourg had considered the case. The bulldozers came at 4am the next day.
tickets.detail: Procedural point: the European Commission of Human Rights application (made 3 May 1988) was still pending; refusing interim protection made the application’s outcome academic for the house.

tickets.what: Inspected the farmhouse for listing on 29 Jul 1988 and declined to list on 5 Dec, the day before the demolition.
tickets.detail: In 2026 Cadw produced only two inspection photographs; the 1988 assessment record has not been produced.

sources.title: GHF-E144 — 1988 Cadw inspection and the 5 December listing decision

tickets.what: Farmhouse demolished: a twenty-strong team with bulldozers moved in just after 4am; by breakfast no building was left standing.
tickets.detail: The family watched. Their application to the European Commission of Human Rights was still pending. “Bulldozed Before Breakfast” (South Wales Echo).

sources.title: Press: “Tears flow as 800 year-old farm house is razed at last” (N11)

tickets.what: Outline permission granted for housing; the officer’s report recorded that the buildings the Local Plan said should be retained had been demolished.
tickets.detail: Outline application 89/01396/OUT, granted with 18 conditions. Appendices B–E of the officer’s report are missing from the file.

tickets.what: Groundworks began before the archaeological condition was met.
tickets.detail: The 1994 excavation that followed lifted an early-medieval cemetery; 814 articulated burials were published in 2005.

tickets.what: Complaint refused at both stages: “no evidence of a mistake in the register”.
tickets.detail: On 10 Oct 2026 HMLR then opened its own application to “investigate and correct any error that may have been made” on WA231076.

tickets.what: FOI 719/26 on the 1988 police and bailiff involvement: “hold no information”.
tickets.detail: A search result, not proof that no operational record ever existed. Internal review 1188/26 is due 26 Oct 2026.

tickets.what: Copies of the 43 first-registration file items offered only by post, on form OC2, at £11 each, paid by cheque.
tickets.detail: 30 items on WA231076 and 13 on WA240304.
